habitat: Lowland dipterocarp forest, freshwater swamp, and tropical peat swamp forests below 500m elevation
description: The Bornean orangutan is Asia's only great ape. Peatland fires destroy the high fruiting canopies they rely upon for food and shelter, forcing mother and infant pairs into fragmented forest patches where human-wildlife conflict increases.

habitat: Primary and secondary rainforests, peat swamp forest margins, and mixed agricultural tree groves
description: An elusive nocturnal mammal covered in protective keratin scales. When subsurface peat fires ignite root cavities, pangolins roll into tight defensive balls rather than fleeing, leaving them trapped by thick smoke and subterranean embers.
story_role: Silent Guardian of the Forest Floor

habitat: Dense tropical evergreen lowland and hill forests, secondary forests
description: The smallest bear species on Earth, recognizable by the radiant amber crescent on its chest. Sun bears rely on mature hardwood hollows for rearing cubs and tear open termite nests and wild bee hives; fires collapse their ancient nesting hollows.

habitat: Dense riverside thickets, lowland dipterocarp understory, and swamp forest fringes
description: A shy, nimble ungulate no larger than a rabbit. Folklore celebrates the mouse deer (Sang Kancil) as quick-witted and agile; yet pervasive regional haze and ground fires eliminate the dense low shrubs and fallen fruit essential for its survival.

threats: loss of large emergent nesting trees
habitat: Pristine lowland and hill evergreen rainforests with tall emergent trees
description: One of the most striking canopy birds in Southeast Asia, known for its loud maniacal call and solid ivory-like casque. Females seal themselves into hollow tree trunks to brood; when peat fire smoke blankets the canopy, nesting families face severe respiratory risk.
